overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance reveals an overwhelming viewer preference for 'What If' scenarios applied to extreme celestial bodies and planetary anomalies. Specifically, hypothetical planetary immersion and extreme planetary properties (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, dark planets, and unusual day-to-year ratios) generate exceptionally high views-per-day and strong engagement (likes-per-view) compared to standard trivia or abstract biology/psychology facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved massive traction with over 900-1,000 views shortly after release, outperforming static declarative statements.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving extreme exoplanets.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Anomalies & Weird Planet Physics
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal planetary conditions like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) drove top-tier views and high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight counter-intuitive physics or bizarre time/weather anomalies on newly discovered or lesser-known celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content focusing on internal human cognition and memory hacks (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' variants) consistently stalled under 60-100 lifetime views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from internal psychological trivia for Shorts unless tied to an immediate, visceral external experiment.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts like octopuses having three hearts saw mixed, lower-tier velocity when framed as simple declarative titles.
weak_patterns.action: Elevate animal concepts into cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic listicle facts.

next_video.concept: What If You Stepped Foot on a Rogue Planet Hurtling Through Interstellar Space?

next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of 'What If' space exploration formats and extreme planetary survival themes.
